history.dynasty: Koch dynasty (later maintained by the Raikats of Baikunthapur)
history.summary: One of the oldest temples of Jalpaiguri district and Bengal. Founded in 1524 by Bisu Singh (Bishwa Singha), king of Cooch Behar and father of Maharaja Nara Narayan; rebuilt by Nara Narayan in 1563 and again by Pran Narayan in 1663. After Mahidev Raikut declared independence from the Koch dynasty in 1621, the temple passed to the supervision of the Raikats of Baikunthapur, and was restored on 30 January 1899 by Rani Jagadeswari Devi, wife of Jagendra Deva Raikut. The temple is dedicated to Bhairava as Jalpesh (a form of Shiva); its famous underground/submerged 'Anadi' shivalinga in the garbhagriha and the Shivratri fair draw hundreds of thousands of pilgrims, including from Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh. Coordinates from geocoder (matched 'Kalpesh Temple' at Maynaguri, consistent with documented location).
